review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset label 1.0 counts as INCLUDE; 0.5 and 0.0 count as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is an observational study analyzing complications from 5,851 consecutively induced abortions. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not compare different surgical methods. The study only analyzes risk factors for complications.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two surgical methods: manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) versus conventional vacuum aspiration (VA). The study randomized 200 women requesting first trimester abortion (gestational age <56 days) to either VA or MVA, meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: This is a historical/trend analysis using population-level mortality and morbidity data from different time periods. It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not compare different surgical methods for abortion.

This is a randomised trial, but it compares prostaglandin cervical preparation versus placebo before vacuum aspiration. The surgical method (vacuum aspiration) is the same in both groups. This study does not compare different surgical methods for abortion.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two different surgical methods: dilatation and curettage (D&C) versus vacuum aspiration (VA). The study randomized 420 women to either D&C or VA for first trimester abortion, meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two surgical methods: manual vacuum aspiration versus electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion. The study randomized 84 women to either method, meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two surgical methods: manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) versus electric vacuum aspiration (EVA) for first trimester abortion. The study randomized women to either MVA (n=64) or EVA (n=63), meeting all selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: This study compares two surgical methods: vacuum aspiration (suction curettage) versus classical dilatation and curettage. While the abstract doesn't explicitly state randomization, it describes a comparative study with 47 women (23 in each group) under nearly identical conditions. Given the conservative screening approach, this study is included pending full-text review to confirm randomisation.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two variations of vacuum aspiration: 8mm metal cannulae versus flexible plastic cannulae for first trimester abortion. While both use vacuum aspiration, they represent different instrument approaches. The study randomized 300 subjects. Given the conservative approach, this is included pending confirmation that this qualifies as comparing different surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised controlled trial comparing two surgical methods: manual vacuum aspirator versus electric vacuum curettage for first trimester abortion. The study randomized 114 women to either technique, meeting all selection criteria.
